# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

The score comes from reading the code ("read from code"), not from a running site. The basics are in place: crawlers are allowed in, the pages use ordinary links, and the sitemap exists. Points are lost on a missing `lang` attribute, a sitemap that `robots.txt` doesn't point to, missing canonicals, and a blog that fills in only in the browser. I sampled 4 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs` and `/blog`. I also read `/thank-you`. It isn't in the sitemap or the menu, and its `noindex` looks deliberate.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** A sitemap is your list of pages. Without a `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt`, crawlers have no pointer to it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` / `User-agent: GPTBot` / `Disallow: /`. There is no `Sitemap:` line anywhere in the file.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100 (earned 18 ÷ 23).

### 2. Add a language to the page
- **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells browsers and machines which language the site is in. Your config says `en`, but the page doesn't.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100 on its own. Together with item 1 it is 87/100 (earned 20 ÷ 23).

### 3. Give every page its own canonical address
- **Why it matters:** A canonical link names the main address of a page. `/docs` and `/blog` have none, so search engines have to guess between duplicate addresses. The `/pricing` canonical points at a page marked `noindex`.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`, `app/blog/page.tsx` (no metadata at all), `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 74/100 if you add canonicals to `/docs` and `/blog` (earned 17 ÷ 23). If `/pricing` also becomes indexable, the canonical and indexability checks both improve and it is 77/100 (earned 18 ÷ 23).

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. `GPTBot` is blocked, which matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. The page is in the sitemap and the menu. 3 of 4 routes are clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Not run | `/` is clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. The `/pricing` canonical target is `noindex`. 1 of 4 routes is clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` has `fetch('/api/posts')` inside `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes are clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Problem | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has `<html>` with no `lang`. Titles and descriptions are present on every route. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has plain `<a href>` links to all four pages |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on a cookie notice (`app/layout.tsx:15`), which is a scoped choice. I found no middleware or `headers()`. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and all five pages. There are no images, and links have text and every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present, and not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present, and not scored |

## Other problems found

None found beyond the scored results above. The `/pricing` `noindex` is scored under GEO-014. It is listed in the sitemap and the menu, so check whether it is intentional.

## Worth considering

- **Block the other training crawlers too:** `geo.config.json`: `"trainingCrawlers": "block"`. `public/robots.txt:4-5` names only `GPTBot`, so the stated policy is applied in part. Add groups for the other training crawlers you want blocked, such as `ClaudeBot`, if you mean the policy to cover all of them.
- **Give blog posts their own pages:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `posts.map((p) => <article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>)`. Each post is only a title with no address of its own. Individual pages with a link from `/blog` might make each post easier to find and quote.
- **Back up the pricing page's promise:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Plans for every team size.'`. The page says only `Free for up to three people.` Listing the plans and prices as text would answer what a visitor comes to learn.
- **Say more in the docs:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The page is one sentence long. A visitor asking how to import a bank feed has no answer in text on the page.
- **Label the business with structured data:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Accounting for small teams`. An `Organization` or `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD block could state what Ledger is in a form machines read directly.

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-003 for `/blog`:** the posts come from `/api/posts`, which isn't in this repository. Whether any server-side data reaches the blog page is outside what I can read.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** real status codes, redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` headers, and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200. A live scan with your URL would confirm these.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- `/thank-you` is meant to be `noindex` and stay out of the sitemap.
- `https://www.ledger.example` is your real domain, from `site.origin` in `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
